### Step 1 — Scene
A mixed plate with a whole Asian pear, a long cooked rib, roasted chicken, a small portion of fried chicken, and one sushi roll piece. The meat identifications are somewhat uncertain.

### Step 2 — Vessel
A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### Steps 3–6 — Items, coverage, volume, and weight
Heights below are average thicknesses across each food’s footprint, rather than maximum heights.

| Visible item | Plate coverage | Area | Average height | Gross volume | Density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Whole Asian pear | 14% | 74 cm² | 4.3 cm | 318 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 286 g |
| Long cooked rib, likely pork | 12% | 64 cm² | 1.7 cm | 109 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 104 g |
| Roasted chicken thigh, skin-on | 13% | 69 cm² | 2.3 cm | 159 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 151 g |
| Fried chicken pieces, including small adjacent scraps | 7% | 37 cm² | 2.0 cm | 74 ml | 0.85 g/ml | 63 g |
| Crab-style sushi roll piece | 3% | 16 cm² | 2.0 cm | 32 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 29 g |

**Coverage check:** 49% total, consistent with roughly half the plate being occupied. No separate pool of sauce or oil is visible; cooking fat and coatings are included in the meat estimates.

### Step 7 — Energy
Using approximate cooked, as-plated energy densities, with allowance for bone in the meat portions:

| Item | kcal/100 g | Estimated kcal |
|---|---:|---:|
| Asian pear | 42 | 120 |
| Cooked rib | 280 | 291 |
| Roasted chicken thigh | 230 | 347 |
| Fried chicken | 290 | 183 |
| Sushi piece | 150 | 44 |

### Step 8 — Sanity check
Estimated total: **633 g and 985 kcal**. The whole pear accounts for almost half the weight, while the meats supply most of the energy. The single sushi piece contributes only about 29 g. A reasonable uncertainty is approximately ±25%, chiefly from meat identity, bone content, and thickness.
